newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans pare gains but end higher on weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans pare gains but end higher on weather.

text.p: Gains were pared late in CBOT soybeans but the market closed higher on concerns persistent dry weather in central Illinois would damage developing crops, trade sources said.
"Gains were off late on perceptions of a little more rain but more important was some folks didn't want to go home too long," said Prudential Securities analyst Tom Levis.

Forecasters said weekend rainfall would be light across central Illinois with thin coverage. Some meteorologists had expected more substantail rainfall but changed their forecasts on Friday after Hurricane Danny moved east instead of north.

"It's all weather-related," said Bill Biedermann, director of research for Allendale Inc. "We're suffering out here, there's no question about it. If we don't get rain this weekend or Monday we'll be sharply higher."

Nearbys were also higher, dragged up by new crop. Traders noted the July contract withstood the 50,000 bushels posted for delivery on Friday. Traders said the market expected the deliveries after the soybeans were registered on Thursday.
Soybeans ended 8-1/2 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with new crop November up 6-3/4 at $6.07-1/2 and July up 1-3/4 at $7.76-1/4.
Gains in the old crop months were capped by the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush data which showed fewer soybeans were crushed this week than last week.

NOPA put the weekly crush at 21.871 million bushels, down from 23.014 million the previous week. The trade had expected a lower crush figure because processors were taking downtime, cash sources said.

Funds were aggressive buyers on the day, accounting for at least 12 million bushels. Cargill Investor Services bought 2.5 million bushels November, Merrill Lynch and Lind-Waldock each bought two million November and Rand Financial and Smith Barney each bought 1.5 million November, pit sources said.
In spread action, Lind-Waldock spread three million August/November at $1.32 to $1.34 premium August, and Tenco Inc spread 1.2 million November/August at $1.38 to $1.32-1/2.

In options trade, Refco Inc sold 800 September $7.25 calls at 10-3/4 cents. Farmers Commodities Corp bought 200 November 700 calls at 13 cents and 200 November $6.50 calls at 19 to 20 cents, traders said.
Volatility in the November was pegged at 25-1/2 percent, compared with Thursday's 23-1/2 percent.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 50,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 48,586 contracts. Options volume was pegged at 24,000 contracts, against Thursday's 26,112.
